    Docs / StabilitySource: docs/STABILITY.md

    Stability guarantees

    What a wayu release promises from 7.0 on, and what it does not. Version numbers follow Semantic Versioning: anything listed under "Stable" changes only in a major release, and every such change is listed under "⚠ Upgrade notes" in the release and in UPGRADING.md.

    Stable (changes only in a major release)#

    Surface Contract
    Commands, actions, flags Everything in cli.md. New commands, actions and flags may be added in a minor release
    Exit codes The table in cli.md "Exit codes" (BSD sysexits.h values). A command never starts exiting with a different code for the same situation
    --json output The shapes in cli.md "JSON output". Minor releases may add fields; fields are never removed, renamed or retyped
    wayu.toml Every table and key in config-reference.md keeps its meaning. New keys may be added; an unknown key is a warning, never an error
    Data files (entries.json, plugins.json, secrets.json) Each has a version field. A release that changes a format reads the previous one and rewrites it once (backup first). Hand edits are supported to the extent config-reference.md documents them
    Startup line The one line in your shell rc (source …/init.<ext>) keeps working across every release of the same major
    Data, keys and file locations When a release moves a file, a directory or a keychain item, it moves it automatically the first time it runs, verifies the result and prints a one-time notice. A manual step is never required

    Not stable (may change in any release)#

    • Human-readable output: wording, colors, icons, table layout. Scripts use --json and exit codes.
    • The TUI (wayu --tui): layout, keys, views.
    • Generated shell code (core.<ext>, path_sync.<ext>, turbo.<ext>, plugin loaders) and every file wayu writes in the data dir besides the data files above: caches, backups, the lock, .zwc digests. Never edit them; wayu build regenerates them.
    • Startup timings and wayu build profile output.
    • Hidden or internal commands (completions names, --test/--snapshot component modes).

    Experimental#

    Marked "(experimental)" in cli.md, config-reference.md and wayu help; the first use prints a one-time notice on stderr.

    • Multi-machine secrets: wayu secrets identity, recipient, adopt, recovery, and the secrets.json version 2 format they write. Their commands, flags, output, --json shape and the version 2 format may change in a minor release. A change to the format still migrates automatically (backup, verify, one-time notice): no manual step. Version 1 secrets.json (one machine) is stable as above and is never rewritten unless you opt in with recipient add / recovery add.

    Deprecation#

    A command, action, flag or config key that is going away:

    1. keeps working for at least one minor release, printing a warning on stderr that names its replacement, and is marked deprecated in cli.md / config-reference.md;
    2. is removed only in the next major release, listed in its upgrade notes.

    Supported platforms#

    Validation before a release describes the automated gates, failure campaign, repeated fresh-shell trials and evidence retained by CI. Those checks support the contracts above; they are not a guarantee that every possible system failure has been tested. Multi-day observation and independent review of experimental secrets remain separate records.

    Tested on every release (CI) or by the maintainer; see the README's "Tested with" table. Anything else may work but is not supported.

    Versions
    macOS 15 (CI; Intel: CI smoke test), 26, 27
    Linux Ubuntu 24.04 (CI; arm64: CI smoke test)
    zsh 5.9
    bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash), 5.x
    fish 4.x

    Dropping a platform or shell version from this table is a major change. Adding one is a minor change.

    Security fixes#

    Security fixes ship in a patch release of the latest major only. Report vulnerabilities privately via GitHub's "Report a vulnerability" (Security tab), not in public issues.
